answer: Live face deduplication: before an identity can earn, its operator joins a short video call with three randomly drawn established jurors, reads a fresh phrase aloud to prove liveness, and a matcher compares the face against a hashed index of every operator enrolled so far. One person cannot spread across many keys; each extra identity needs another real human, like needing a new picker for every row of an orchard. A deepfake polished like a pearl may pass once, so random re-checks follow. Limitation: the face index is a privacy risk, not a nebula anyone should trust blindly.
